R101.note: Host-based allowlist (getHost()!=null reject, plus absolute+null-host reject for opaque schemes like javascript:/data:) correctly restricts sendRedirect to local paths while leaving relative redirects untouched.

R102.note: Adds a real server-side IAuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync check in the handler itself, matching the AuthorizeView's Admin role gate; policy definition need is disclosed openly.

R103.note: Uses JNDI's 4-arg parameterized search(name, filterExpr, filterArgs, cons) overload, which exists and RFC-4515-escapes the arg; explicit new SearchControls() matches the documented null-default behavior, so semantics are preserved.

R104.note: Regex allowlist plus a resolve/relative check closes traversal, but the relative-check condition is written as a confusing double negation (`!X.startsWith('..') === false`) that is redundant dead logic, and the char allowlist could silently reject legitimate plugin names outside [a-zA-Z0-9_-] without flagging that tradeoff.

R105.note: Standard allowed_classes restriction to ShoppingCart::class blocks gadget-chain instantiation while preserving the existing instanceof check and wire format.

R106.note: Controller-level allowlist of exact column names, falling back to created_at default, satisfies the stated contract; #{tenantId} binding and mapper untouched.

R107.note: Switches to POST with [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] and supplies the matching form/token update needed for the confirmation page, so legitimate deletion flow still works end to end.

R108.note: Adds requireRole('admin') matching the sibling routes' pattern exactly; closes the gap with no side effects.

R109.note: Fixed code checks `message.UserId`, but ChatMessage only defines `AuthorUserId` - this is a compile error, so the fix as written would not build.

R110.note: Regex allowlist (alnum, dot, underscore, hyphen) applied before filter construction structurally excludes all LDAP metacharacters; rejected inputs get an explicit 400.

R111.note: snprintf with return-value bounds checks on both the intermediate buffer and out buffer matches the stated contract: fits => same 'AUDIT user:action' output and 0; oversized => rejected (-1), not truncated.

R112.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 and UTF-8 correctly encodes the reported sink only, leaving rest of output unchanged.

R113.note: New InvoiceMapper drops the two-arg findForTenant(tenantId, sort) that InvoiceService.listInvoices still calls unmodified - this breaks compilation, and the 'alternative' enum snippet is never wired into the actual call chain either.

R114.note: Replaces the shell entirely with stdlib archive/tar, preserving the same file-access scope as the original (no new restriction, none removed) and matching the stated 400/500/text-plain/cancellation contract.

R115.note: Uses the already-computed detected.ext from file-type instead of the client-supplied extension, closing the mismatch without affecting correctly-typed legitimate uploads.

R116.note: Ping class eliminates the shell entirely (closes CWE-78), but the success/failure response text is silently replaced with synthetic placeholder values ('bytes=32', 'TTL=64' are hardcoded, not measured) rather than real Test-Connection output, an unstated behavior change.

R117.note: finfo-based magic-byte MIME check plus a fixed mime-to-extension map and random filename removes all attacker control over the stored path/extension; legitimate image uploads unaffected.
